title: sklearn2c
tagline: Transpile fitted scikit-learn models to dependency-free C for microcontrollers, verified sample by sample against the compiled code.
problem: scikit-learn does not run on microcontrollers, and runtimes such as TFLite Micro or ONNX add flash, RAM and a toolchain. Hand-porting a model to C is error-prone: the original transpiler returned class indices instead of labels and its 'verification' never executed the C.
approach: sklearn2c reads the fitted parameters (tree nodes, forest tables, coefficients) and emits C99 with them as const data and a single predict(const float *x). Leaves map through classes_, tree thresholds are emitted as the largest float32 <= the float64 threshold so routing is bit-identical to sklearn, and verify_predictions compiles the C with gcc, calls it through ctypes and compares every sample, including inputs exactly on each split.

demo.caption: Live terminal run: train a fault classifier with labels 10/20/30, export it to C, compile it with gcc, check parity on held-out data, print the parity table for every supported model, then show the clear error raised for string labels.

limits: Integer class labels only (int32); string labels must be encoded with LabelEncoder first.
Linear models accumulate in float by default; inputs within float rounding of the decision boundary can flip label (compile with -DSKLEARN2C_REAL=double for exact parity).
Forest classifiers accumulate probabilities in double to match sklearn exactly; this is software-emulated on Cortex-M4F.
No Pipeline / preprocessing export, no NaN (missing value) routing, no gradient boosting, SVM kernels or MLPs.
Latency measured on an x86 VM, not on a microcontroller; ARM builds are compiled and linked, not run.
